title: Principality of Theodoro
capsule: The Principality of Theodoro (capital: Mangup/Doros) was a Greek Orthodox principality in the mountainous southwestern Crimea, emerging in the early 14th century from Byzantine successor politics after Mongol disruption, with the earliest recorded ruler Demetrios noted around 1362/3. At its apex under Alexios I (c. 1410–1444), Theodoro challenged Genoese commercial dominance at Caffa and allied with Moldavia through a dynastic marriage to Stephen the Great. Ottoman commander Gedik Ahmed Pasha besieged Mangup from September 1475; the fortress surrendered in December after months of famine. The last prince, Alexander, was transported to Constantinople and executed, and his family was absorbed into the sultan's court.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The principality's highland core at Mangup is archaeologically well documented; control over coastal strips and the boundary with the Crimean Khanate's steppe territories are not precisely delimited in contemporary sources.
